W.note: Release's slow first fifth gives a real grip and Press has a strong attack, with a graph, tags and peak/settle readouts, but Pause/Play is broken under reduced motion because the CSS media rule keeps the dots paused after Play is pressed, and Press and Catch overlap in character.

X.note: Three distinct curves and correct values, but there is no graph, no reading copy, no pause control and no reduced-motion handling, and the Punchy Overshoot and Sticky Punch balls visibly overhang the track ends.

Y.note: The bare track-and-ball layout with copyable values is clean but never says which curve is sticky or punchy, shows no graph or readouts, and ignores reduced motion and pausing entirely.

Z.note: The shared 1.6 s clock with explicit forward, hold, pass-back and rest phases makes the grip visibly linger and gives seamless loops, and it pairs a graph playhead with readouts, starts paused under reduced motion, and has a working Pause/Play, though its readouts omit settle time.
